# 2 Baruch Chapter 32 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Second Fast and Dialogue

---

**1** For whatever is now is nothing; but whatever is coming will be great. For all that is corruptible will pass away, and everything that dies will depart, and every present time will be forgotten, and there will be no remembrance of the present age, because that which comes is coming quickly.

**2** For the souls of the righteous who are now in distress know what has been prepared for them, and on account of this they will not be distressed.

**3** But as for us — if we did not know that we are in distress, we would have understood nothing; for we know that the distress of this world will not last.

**4** And I said to them further: Will not all these distresses pass away from us? And will there not come a time of rest for us? And behold — Zion will be built up again, and the offerings will be restored, and the priests will return to their place, and the peoples will return to the land.

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal equivalence rendering. The contrast between the passing present and the coming eternal age is the rhetorical engine of this chapter. The promise of Zion's rebuilding (v.4) is a historical-eschatological hope — a rebuilt second Zion before the final end.*
